concerns.text: T012 mandates 'continuous 5-minute epochs' for Welch's PSD. This contradicts Constitution Principle VI and Spec FR-003 which explicitly define the method as '5-minute epochs, 2-s windows'. The task description in T012 incorrectly states '4-second windows' in the body text while the spec/constitution requires 2-second windows. This is a semantic weakening of the preprocessing constraint.

T010a defines bad channel rejection as 'variance exceeding a statistically significant threshold' and requires a config value `BAD_CHANNEL_THRESHOLD_STD`. Spec FR-002 and Plan Phase 1 explicitly require rejecting channels with variance '> 3 SD' (or a specific statistical threshold defined in the plan). The task's reliance on a generic 'statistically significant' check without enforcing the specific 3-SD invariant from the plan/spec creates a risk of silent drift where the exclusion criteria are not met.

T022a describes a permutation test that 'evaluates the pre-trained model' on shuffled data without re-training. Spec FR-007 and Plan Phase 2 require a permutation test to assess the significance of the model's R². Standard permutation testing for model significance (to avoid overfitting bias) requires re-training the model on shuffled labels to generate the null distribution. Evaluating a fixed model on shuffled data tests the model's robustness to noise, not the statistical significance of the learned relationship. This semantic drift invalidates the statistical claim in FR-007.

T004 mandates raising a ValueError if `OVERLAP` is not set, citing 'Spec is [deferred]'. However, Spec FR-003 and Constitution Principle VI explicitly define the overlap as '50% overlap' (or '2-s windows' implying a specific overlap). The task treats a defined parameter as '[deferred]' and forces a manual override, violating the spec's explicit definition of the preprocessing parameters. The spec does not defer overlap; it defines it.

T010c excludes participants if 'ratio of rejected channels exceeds 0.30'. Spec FR-002 states 'If >30% of channels are rejected... the participant MUST be excluded'. The task uses 'exceeds 0.30' (strictly > 0.30) while the spec says '>30%'. While mathematically similar, the task description in T010a/b/c context implies a hard stop at 30%. The phrasing 'exceeds 0.30' is technically correct for >30%, but the task must ensure the exclusion logic matches the spec's 'hard stop' requirement exactly. More critically, T010c is marked as [P] (parallel) but depends on T010b (sequential). The dependency graph in the task list is inconsistent with the [P] tag, risking execution order violations.
